authority: #K2-476 sec.3.2 (read-only audit window: name the break for I2C2_SCL / GND across the post-maze stages; check whether the 27 escape ports worsened the no-op count). Zero board writes; zero exam runs; zero generator changes.
method: for each chain stage board, enumerate the net's copper objects and measure the nearest endpoint to the pad, to the escape-port, and to the frame-port track. BEFORE = /tmp/opencode/k2w1/s3c_disposed.kicad_pcb (pre-B), AFTER = /tmp/opencode/k2b1/s3c_disposed.kicad_pcb (post-B).

named_break.layer: the MAZE'S PORT SEMANTICS (a port is an extra GOAL for its net) - not a copper layer
named_break.stage: M2 maze (k2_reroute_router_floor_v1) - NOT the stitch/refill/dispose stages
named_break.object: the 27 escape ports registered by R1540 (#K2-475 B)
named_break.why: an escape port sits 0.8mm from the pad, while the edge's REAL endpoint (the frame-port track) is 13.76mm away. With the escape port in the goal set the maze satisfies the edge with a trivial 0.8mm stub and reports blocked=[] - the 13.76mm route is never attempted.

the_two_objects: PCB_TRACK F.Cu (37.75,57.962)->(37.75,57.163)  <-- DUPLICATE: two identical overlapping segments
AFTER_B_k2b1.note: the corridor WAS laid as copper - from the escape port to the pad - i.e. exactly the 0.8mm false goal. The frame-port distance is unchanged and the DRC still reports the pad <-> 9.3mm frame-port track as UNCONNECTED.

audit_item_2_answer: YES - the 27 escape ports WORSE this. They converted genuine routing failures into FALSE SUCCESSES: the residual maze pass now reports blocked=[] and reasons={} (R1540's machine evidence) precisely because the edge is 'solved' by a 0.8mm stub to the escape port, while C1 stays 2. So the R1540 machine criterion was satisfied in a way that HIDES the failure.
consequence: the residual is a maze PORT-SEMANTICS defect introduced by R1540's B, not a stitch/refill/dispose break. The real edge endpoint (the frame port) must be the goal; the escape corridor may serve as a START, not as a GOAL.
next_candidates: 1. RESTRICT the escape ports: register them as START-only / do not add them to the maze's goal set (or require the edge's own endpoint to be reached). Deterministic, bounded, zero geometry.
2. remove the duplicate overlapping segments (a cosmetic wart in the same area).
3. C6 (800 vs legacy 2) as the separate piece.
